content.text: The solve succeeded. The largest displacement is 0.7165 mm. I look at the results folder to see if it also gives the z-displacement at the tip.

The FEA tip deflection is 0.7165 mm down. Timoshenko beam theory gives 0.7217 mm, so the FEA value is 0.7 % lower.

**Commands**
- `fh-python part.py` writes `part.step`.
- `fh info part.step --case .` shows that the units match (SI-mm).
- `fh run . --size 2.5` makes 3639 C3D10 elements and 6695 nodes. The solve took 2.8 s, and its status is ok.

**Results folder:** `/tmp/fh-state/projects/p-c80e4cdf0c7f0d39/runs/run-000001/out`. The viewer of the page shows run-000001.

**Comparison** (q = p × b = 10 N/mm, I = 833.3 mm⁴, E = 210000 MPa)

| Source | Tip deflection (mm) | FEA difference |
|---|---|---|
| FEA, largest displacement | 0.7165 | — |
| Euler-Bernoulli, qL⁴/(8EI) | 0.7143 | +0.3 % |
| Timoshenko, with the shear part | 0.7217 | −0.7 % |

The FEA value is between the two beam values. The fixed face at x = 0 also stops the Poisson contraction, and this makes the model a little stiffer than a beam.

The run output gives only the largest displacement magnitude, which is at a tip corner. It includes approximately 0.002 mm of axial movement, so the z-deflection alone is about 0.715 mm. I could not open the results folder from this session, so I did not read the mean z-deflection of the tip face.

**Changes to the case template:** `fh` did not accept the template as it was. A class N case also needs these items:
- `derivation`
- `mesh = ["part.inp"]`
- `rel_tol` and `abs_tol`
- `[ref]` and a `[quantity.*]` table

I added these items. The reference is the Timoshenko value, and the tolerance is 5 %. `derivation.md` contains the hand calculation.

result: The FEA tip deflection is 0.7165 mm down.
